reserveReview.rationale: Current-block refresh on 2026-09-29: at Ethereum block 26,083,711 (timestamp 2026-09-29T14:26:11Z, pinned JSON-RPC reads), the pmUSD Treasury (0x51c4348af0c6066a2fd31bd968bc0c039fe27342) returned TokenBlender (0x7a7f847fb60b0000e24cce07298dc73df8b8e56a) from baseToken(). The TokenBlender proxy is a Blockscout-verified EIP-1967 transparent proxy with implementation 0xd38D289dC319311015E6526F56C15DA078E41aaE, and its getSupportedTokens() still returns exactly one token, ION.au (0xd051c326c9aef673428e6f01eb65d2c52de95d30). At the same pinned block, Treasury balanceOf(TokenBlender) returned 26,528.785212665816068303 TB, while getTokenReserveBalance(ION.au) and TokenBlender totalSupply each returned exactly 26,531.98 units of the 18-decimal token; the reserve balance equals total supply, so every TB unit is backed by ION.au, and the Treasury holding is an ION.au-backed position whose gap from aggregate TB supply reflects only units held outside the Treasury. The direct pmUSD reserve path therefore remains a single 100% TokenBlender position backed solely by ION.au, unchanged from the 2026-08-29 enumeration at block 25,862,798. RAAC's pmusd.raac.io collateral page sat behind a Vercel security checkpoint (HTTP 429) on 2026-09-29 and could not be re-opened from the research vantage; the 2026-08-29 reading of that disclosure remains the corroborating issuer statement, and the Chainlink ION proof-of-reserve feed stays corroborative for I-ON's broader reserve. Neither resolves the legal enforceability, valuation, extraction costs, or recovery liquidity of the underlying in-situ gold claims.
